A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGMatch study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SGMatch benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, repeated-seed experiments and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds regularizer comparisons, transport-field analysis, semantic-backbone and view-count experiments, and preprocessing timings.

M1.justification: The proposed feature extractors, gated local attention, functional-map solver, heat diffusion and CFM training objective remain unchanged. The revised CFM explanation and additional experimental variants do not establish a change to SGMatch's algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate full-shape correspondence on FAUST, SCAPE, SHREC’19, SMAL, DT4D-H and TOPKIDS. New analyses use this retained coverage; no additional dataset, population or matching task is evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds a dedicated comparison against endpoint-only, cycle-consistency and synchronous-diffusion-style objectives within the same SGMatch backbone on SMAL and TOPKIDS (Section 5.5, Table 3). This substantially expands controls for the central CFM contribution. The external methods in the main benchmark comparisons remain unchanged; the new objectives are not evaluations of entire cited systems.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands beyond geodesic error and conformal distortion to coverage, Dirichlet energy, bijectivity and neighbor velocity deviation. New experiments vary regularization objectives, semantic backbones and rendered-view counts. The reported TOPKIDS diffusion time changes from 0.01 to 0.1 (Appendix A.2), while dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of CFM versus alternative objectives, quantitative transport-field coherence, a gating-only ablation, and semantic-backbone and view-count sensitivity. These substantially broaden investigation of the method's mechanisms and dependencies. The local-attention-without-gating result is retained from v1 Appendix B.1 and moved into v2 Table 4, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The three seeds (42, 1234 and 3407), mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and numerical statistical table are retained from v1 Appendix F/Table 10 to v2 Appendix G/Table 15. No additional repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for map-quality metrics, alternative regularizers, transport coherence, semantic backbones, view counts and preprocessing costs. TOPKIDS headline error changes from 3.3 to 2.9 and PCK AUC from 0.88 to 0.89 alongside the changed diffusion setting; 2.9 already appeared in v1's diffusion sweep. Table 1 swaps the DT4D-H intra/inter headings without changing cell values, altering their reported task association. Figure 7 removes the FAUST, SCAPE and SHREC’19 distortion curves/AUCs. Most other headline accuracy results and the repeated-seed results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix D.1 adds Equation (22), mathematically defining neighbor velocity deviation and specifying learned velocities for CFM versus endpoint displacements without CFM. The existing mathematical formulation is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: semantic guidance resolves descriptor ambiguity, CFM promotes spatial coherence, and SGMatch performs competitively near isometry with stronger benefits under deformation and topological noise. Rewording CFM as an adapted transport regularizer does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 replaces v1's asserted equivalence between velocity consistency and non-divergent neighboring trajectories with an explicitly implicit spatial prior arising from heat-smoothed endpoints and a shared finite-capacity network. New discussion acknowledges mixed regularity metrics and interprets cycle-consistency's lower TOPKIDS Dirichlet energy as possible over-smoothing. The existing partial-matching and semantic-generalization limitations are retained and modestly clarified.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix H newly separates one-time semantic-feature extraction from pairwise inference, reports extraction costs of 34.7–109.4 seconds per shape, and explains caching. Appendix A.2 updates the TOPKIDS diffusion parameter. Hardware, optimizer, feature dimensions and most implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to S3M, Spectral Meets Spatial and Surface-Aware Distilled 3D Semantic Features, and removes Geometrically Consistent Partial Shape Matching. Related work more explicitly discusses diffusion-based smoothness, spectral-spatial interpolation and semantic-feature extraction, without substantially changing the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, contribution summary, related work, CFM explanation and experimental discussion. Limitations become a separate section, the appendix analysis gains subsections, and acknowledgements and author details are added. The overall narrative and main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially expanded with multi-metric comparison tables and new tables for transport coherence, backbone/view sensitivity and preprocessing cost. The main ablation table gains explicit gating and attention columns and descriptive variant names. Figure 7 contracts from six panels to three, Table 1's intra/inter headers are exchanged, and several displays move or receive shorter captions; existing qualitative shape images are retained.

improvement.justification: The controlled regularizer comparisons, complementary map-quality metrics and more qualified CFM explanation strengthen assessment of the central smoothness claim. Reporting semantic preprocessing cost also improves transparency. These gains are moderated by reporting problems: v2's claim of the best DT4D-H intra-class result contradicts Table 1 (1.0 versus 0.9 for ULRSSM and DeepFAFM), and the unchanged TOPKIDS three-seed result of 3.36 ± 0.06 is not reconciled with the changed default and 2.9 headline result.
